parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਭੁਰਜੀ (bhurjī), ultimately from Sanskrit भृज्जति (bhṛjjati, “roasts, fries”). Related to fry and bhujia.

parole.significato: A double-edged sword from India, used ceremonially in Sikhism.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਖੰਡਾ (khaṇḍā), from Sanskrit खड्ग (khaḍga).

parole.significato: A ceremonial sword that must be worn at all times by baptized Sikhs, and one of the five Ks.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਕਿਰਪਾਨ (kirpān), from Sanskrit कृपाण (kṛpāṇa, “sword, dagger, sacrificial knife”), from कल्पयति (kalpáyati, “he orders, apportions, cuts, trims”).

parole.significato: Attachment to the transient material world, which hinders the soul's search for its ultimate goal and is therefore one…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਮੋਹ (moh), itself borrowed from Sanskrit मोह (moha).

parole.significato: A bearded reddish sheep, subspecies of Ovis orientalis (including Ovis orientalis vignei), previously classified as Ovi…
